populate the eight parallel radix-2 butterfly lanes (one per BRAM bank) by wiring each DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register; finally seat the four carbon-fiber radix-4 fusion yokes in the open gap between the multiplier and add/sub columns, each binding a lane-pair (0-1, 2-3, 4-5, 6-7) into one fused 4-input radix-4 butterfly unit so the eight radix-2 lanes reconfigure into four radix-4 BUs. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member abutting it, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar (grounded by a standoff post onto the reduction member), and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column (grounded by its own standoff onto the array frame), keeping the read, return and twiddle channels on three separate heights; cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the elevated rail spanning the multiplier column (grounded by a standoff onto the array frame) so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers;
